name: JFLint
description: Adds endpoints for library defects that /Items cannot filter for, starting with episodes whose season could not be determined.
overview: Library-lint queries the Jellyfin API cannot express.

versions.changelog: Adds the UnflattenedRelease / UnflattenedReleaseDB pair: release folders that give every episode its own directory, the layout that has to be flattened before Jellyfin can read the season. One row per release folder with the number of per-episode folders it holds. It is not the same question as PerEpisodeFolder, which names a season Jellyfin created whose name looks like a file name - the child; this names the release folder holding at least three of them - the parent - and derives it from episode paths alone, so it holds whether or not Jellyfin resolved anything. A configured library location is refused however well it fits the shape, because three single-episode releases directly beneath one are enough to qualify it and a caller would then be offered a whole library to flatten. The threshold is a parameter defaulting to three and is refused below two, where every folder holding a single episode would make its parent a release. Both halves share one rule, take the same base population by construction, and the database half expands the stored path before grouping rather than before reporting - the grouping is on the path, so a placeholder would produce a different parent and not merely a different string.

OrphanRowsDB gains TableRows, which is the previous release's own argument one level down. A foreign key on an EMPTY table reports zero violations - correctly, and meaninglessly, because an empty table cannot produce one. Without the row count beside it that zero reads exactly like a zero measured over a quarter of a million rows, and two of the seventeen relations on the reference server are that shape. The count comes from one assembled UNION ALL over the table names in sqlite_master, which is unavoidable rather than convenient: SQLite has no catalogue view carrying row counts and a table name cannot be a parameter. The names are the database's own and are quoted by SQLite's rules anyway, measured against a table deliberately named with an embedded quote and with the control that the unquoted form is rejected.

Adds GET /JFLint/OrphanRowsDB: rows whose parent row is gone, one line per declared foreign key, plus the tables that declare none and are therefore outside the check. On the reference library PRAGMA foreign_key_check reports 202,806 such rows across ten tables, every one pointing at BaseItems - and that single parent is a finding rather than a property of the schema, since four of those tables can reference a second parent and none of those sides is violated. It is not a broken cascade: the constraints carry ON DELETE CASCADE and it fires, measured on both lines. Orphans come from a window in which enforcement is off, which is ordinary because SQLite cannot alter a constraint in place and a table rebuild runs with foreign keys disabled. The rows with nothing to report are included on purpose: a foreign key with no violations returns zero, a table declaring none returns null, and rendering both as an empty list would be a check that cannot fail. This route has no object-model twin because none can exist - the rows are defined by their parent being gone, so there is nothing for the library side to return.

Adds the ImageInfo / ImageInfoDB route pair: findings about the rows that describe an item's images - an image described by more than one row, an image whose stored width or height is zero, and an image with no blurhash. Duplicate rows make every library scan stat the same file again and again, and the stock API cannot show them in bulk: BaseItemDto.ImageTags is keyed by image type and holds one entry per type, so a row that exists thousands of times looks like one that exists once. Per item the server can answer, but only one item per call. One finding per image rather than per row, each carrying how many rows it covers. Both halves report the expanded path, because an image path is stored with Jellyfin's %MetadataPath% placeholder and most artwork lives there. The blurhash test asks for length rather than comparing the column against an empty string, which cannot match a blob in SQLite at all.

Corrects the evidence given in the previous entry. The uniqueid mechanism is real, but the library TvRage ids never demonstrated it: Jellyfin built-in TMDb provider writes them from the external_ids cross-reference, setting Tvdb, Imdb and TvRage but no Tmdb id of its own, which is exactly the key set those episodes carry. Adds two measured facts for callers: an NFO can set and overwrite a provider id but never remove one, and the type attribute must match the stored spelling exactly - a second entry differing only in case makes PowerShell reject the whole response at HTTP 200 with valid JSON.

Corrects the previous entry: an NFO can carry these keys after all. BaseNfoParser skips an unknown element name such as anidbid, but its uniqueid branch looks up the type attribute and stores it verbatim when no provider is registered - no validation at all. That is how 9,575 TvRage ids reached a server on which the provider has never been installed, one of them reading 1065779330. The route remarks now warn that a value set here is a database edit and a later rescan will restore the old one from the file, so repairing the NFO is the durable fix.

Corrects a claim that shipped in the previous catalogue entry. SetProviderId is not the only way to change a provider id: Jellyfin POST /Items/{itemId} rebuilds the whole dictionary from its body, so a key left out is gone. The real argument for a separate route is narrower - that same UpdateItem writes 25 further fields straight from the body with no null guard, including Name, Overview, Genres and LockedFields, so a partial body blanks them. A route that can touch nothing but provider ids needs no proof that a full round trip is lossless.

Adds POST /JFLint/SetProviderId, which sets one provider id on named rows or removes it when no value is given. This is the only way such a value can be changed: the NFO parser only reads elements whose provider is installed, so an anime id in a tvshow.nfo is skipped on every read. Setting a non-numeric value such as none keeps the name-search suppression a sentinel provided while letting a consumer that parses ids numerically drop the field instead of sending it. The finding routes now judge a value by whether it parses as an unusable number rather than by its shape, because provider ids are strings and only the ones that look like numbers cause harm.

Adds GET /JFLint/InvalidProviderIds and the DB twin - provider ids that cannot identify anything, one row per id, for movies, series and episodes - plus POST /JFLint/RemoveProviderId, which removes named providers from named rows. Jellyfin never deletes a provider id on a refresh and both public setters refuse a blank value, so nothing over HTTP could take one out. The judgement is per provider: a single numeric predicate reports 678 values across 512 of 527 series on the reference library, because TvdbSlug is text by design and Custom is opaque, while the per-provider rule reports the 192 that are actually wrong.

Fixes MediaInfoDB on Jellyfin 12: 1118 Dolby Vision files were reported as DOVIInvalid while the server itself answered DOVIWithHDR10 for the same items. Jellyfin 12 added a validation step that also requires the bt2020nc colour space and bt2020 primaries, and this route was not reading those two columns. Proven against both package lines with identical inputs, and harmless on 10.11. The net10.0 build now also compiles against the final 12.0.0 packages instead of a release candidate.

Ports the hyphen branch of the shared file-name rule from the calling tool: a release name separated by hyphens rather than dots - tvr-lots-s02e01 - carries no dot and was invisible to FileNameTitle. The hyphen half additionally requires lower case, which separates scene releases from real German compound titles without exception. Also widens the database half pre-filter, which would otherwise have dropped exactly those rows before the rule saw them while the library half reported them.

Adds GET /JFLint/EpisodeShapedMovie and the DB twin: an item resolved as a film whose file name carries a season and episode number - one episode of a series filed as a movie, which a mixed library produces per folder. Previously visible only where such episodes happened to collide into a duplicate group; one of the four folders on the reference library produced no collision and was invisible. The judgement is on the file name rather than the folder, measured: a folder criterion would have added two false rows and no true ones.

Adds GET /JFLint/ImplausibleGroupingKey and its database twin: series that Jellyfin merged onto one grouping key built from an id that cannot be a real one, such as a sentinel written into two NFOs to prevent a merge and matching itself instead. Sharing a key is normal and is not reported. What counts as a real id differs per provider, and a custom id is opaque by design and never reported.

The duplicate routes now order their rows by item id as the final key. Path was the last key before, and it is not unique - two entries pointing at one file is exactly what a duplicate finder reports - so rows that matched on every other key could come back in different orders from the two halves of the pair.

Adds GET /JFLint/MediaInfoDB: width, height, video range and video range type for every movie and episode with a video stream, in a single database join. The stock API cannot return the colour range without shipping every media stream of every item. The classification itself is Jellyfin own, taken from its public GetVideoColorRange method rather than reimplemented.

ItemsByPathDB now searches one range per stored path root, so it also agrees with ItemsByPath for a directory that contains Jellyfin metadata or data directory rather than lying inside it - the previous release corrected only the case at or below them. Both halves also take an item type name from the same table, so the same row is no longer labelled two ways.

Every database-backed route now reports the same paths as its library-backed twin: Jellyfin stores the metadata and data directories as placeholders, and only one route expanded them back. Also gives the episodes-without-season pair a shared row order, so its two halves can be compared line by line.

ItemsByPathDB now compares against the path Jellyfin actually stores, so it no longer answers with nothing for items below the metadata and data directories - its result matches ItemsByPath again. Both path routes accept either the real or the placeholder spelling of a directory and return the same set for each.

Keeps the file-name-title rule level with the tool that defines it: 4k now counts as a release marker, alongside the resolutions the pattern already knew. Measured to change no finding on the reference library - it closes a gap rather than moving a number.

Two new checks. FileNameTitle lists entries whose title is nothing but the file or folder they came from, which is what anyone opening the library actually sees. PerEpisodeFolder lists seasons that are really one episode's own directory, from releases that give each episode a folder - Jellyfin turns each of those into a season, so one series shows twenty. Both arrive as new kinds on the existing findings shape, so a caller needs no new parser.

Corrects 11.8.0.0, which cleared the wrong copy of the library folders. A query made without a user context is answered from the aggregate root, and that keeps its own objects for those folders rather than the ones reached by id - so the previous release dropped a listing nothing was reading. Both are dropped now, which also brings the two views back onto one set of objects.

A library entry removed through the plugin no longer keeps turning up in queries until the server is restarted. Jellyfin drops its cached folder listing for the parent it resolves by id, which is a different object from the one a user-less query actually walks, so the removal succeeded and the entry stayed visible. Adds POST /JFLint/ForgetCachedChildren to clear entries stranded that way earlier, or by a route that knows nothing about this.

Every field a route declares is now sent on every row, null where unset. Jellyfin omits null properties from its JSON, so a field that applied to no row was missing entirely rather than present and empty - which a caller cannot tell apart from a field the plugin fails to send. Affects all response types, not just the one that prompted it.

Fixes the duplicate routes filtering empty strings differently on their two halves, which could have grouped unrelated rows into one bucket. Clarifies that the presentation-key branch of the movie identity groups files already linked as alternate versions and is not a fallback for movies without a provider id.

Adds DuplicateEpisode and DuplicateMovie, each with a database twin: the same content held twice across different folders, which the stock API cannot answer because the only sound grouping key is not exposed on BaseItemDto.
The 409 from DeleteItemKeepFile now names the descendants that block the removal - id, type, name and path - alongside the exact count, instead of reporting the count alone.

Adds DeleteItemKeepFile: removes one library entry and leaves the media file on disk. The stock delete route hardcodes file deletion and does not expose the flag over HTTP. Takes no parameter, refuses a folder that still has descendants, and never deletes recursively.

Fixes ItemsByPath answering 500 on libraries holding rows whose item type no longer resolves to a class. Both path routes now name the item kinds explicitly, so they also keep returning the same set as each other.

Adds ItemsByPath: every item at a given path plus everything beneath it, over ILibraryManager and straight from the database. Lets a caller turn a file or folder path into an item id without reading the whole library.

Fixes SeriesWithoutFilesDB, which took 15.8 s: BaseItems has no index on SeriesId, so the correlated subquery cost one table scan per series. Replaced by a single grouped pass over the episode rows. The answer is unchanged.

Adds five library-layout findings: phantom seasons, season folders without video, duplicate season numbers, series that yielded no playable file, and rows pointing at a parent that no longer exists. Each is available over ILibraryManager and straight from the database.
Reproducible build. Behaviour unchanged from the previous release.
First release: EpisodesWithoutSeason and EpisodesWithoutSeasonDB.
